facility_roles.quote: The detector is located at the Fenton Hill site of Los Alamos National Laboratory, about 35 miles west of Los Alamos, NM

intervals.label: construction
intervals.note: The start of construction is not given in any source fetched; the pond was completed in early 1999.
intervals.quote: The construction of the Milagro pond was completed in early 1999, and operations began in mid 1999.

intervals.label: operation
intervals.note: Start: the status paper says operations began in mid 1999 and the pond has operated continuously since January 2000; the 2011 Crab paper and the HAWC design paper state "operated from 2000 to 2008". The 1999 start is kept; the end is 2008 in both.
intervals.quote: The construction of the Milagro pond was completed in early 1999, and operations began in mid 1999.

intervals.label: data taking ended
intervals.note: The central reservoir was operated alone from 2000 to 2004, after which the outrigger array was added (arXiv:1110.0409).

name: Milagro
notes: Successor: the HAWC design paper (arXiv:1310.0074) calls Milagro "HAWCs predecessor" and reuses its 900 R5912 photomultipliers; the lineage row (predecessor) is on experiment:hawc.
The prototype Milagrito (before the pond) is mentioned in arXiv:astro-ph/0110513 but is not a separate Atlas record.
No INSPIRE experiment id is recorded: INSPIRE was not contacted by this stream.

physics_goals.quote: Milagro is ideally suited to monitor the variable TeV Universe and discover new sources of TeV gamma rays.
physics_goals.value: Monitor the variable TeV sky continuously with an all-sky water-Cherenkov array and discover new sources of TeV gamma rays.

summary.plain: A huge covered pond of water in the mountains of New Mexico, lined with light sensors, that watched the whole overhead sky day and night for TeV gamma rays and cosmic rays from 1999 until 2008. Its sensors were later reused in HAWC.
summary.technical: Water-Cherenkov extensive-air-shower observatory at Fenton Hill (Jemez Mountains, 2630 m): a 60 m x 80 m x 8 m pond with 723 PMTs in two layers plus an outrigger tank array, sensitive to about 100 GeV-100 TeV primaries over the whole overhead sky. Operations mid-1999 to 2008; successor HAWC.

unique_capabilities.quote: is the world's first large-area water Cherenkov detector capable of continuously monitoring the entire sky for sources of TeV gamma rays
unique_capabilities.value: A water-Cherenkov air-shower array that continuously monitors the entire overhead sky in the TeV band, day and night, unlike pointed Cherenkov telescopes.
